title: Vendor the minimal verified MIT YEIS universe-model closure behind a Personal Universe adapter

scope.subject: Universe data/model layer migration from local V2 generators to the selected YEIS MIT core

research_summary: Phase 1 of the accepted mother-backbone decision will not import the full YEIS application. A dependency-closure scan from Universe, StarSystem, CelestialBody and StarCatalog found only 22 TypeScript files. A clean-room compatibility copy of that closure compiles with this project's Three 0.185.1 after two intentional host adaptations: replace the upstream UI i18n module with an identity/Intl compatibility shim and replace the Vite-injected __BUILD_ID__ cache key with the pinned upstream SHA. The HYG-derived binary is only 2.63 MB plus 201 KB names and contains 109,401 stars. Choose exact vendoring of the minimal closure plus a narrow Personal Universe adapter and optional diagnostic loader. Reject a full app fork/iframe, a Git submodule of the entire repository, and rewriting the algorithms into local V2 code because those options either preserve unnecessary product coupling or forfeit the main reuse benefit.

sources.finding: The selected reproducible MIT snapshot contains the exact Universe/StarSystem/StarCatalog/SystemGenerator source used by the minimal closure and is the only permitted upstream source boundary for this migration.

The snapshot documents the HYG-derived stars.bin as CC BY-SA 4.0 and distinguishes NASA/JPL and other third-party material, so vendoring must preserve notices and avoid copying unrelated branded/media assets.

Git submodules pin an external repository commit in a superproject, but require explicit submodule initialization/update and would bring repository-level coupling when this task only needs a 22-file closure.
Astro supports framework islands, so the selected core can remain behind the existing React client shell rather than replacing the site application.
ProceduralPlanets remains an optional renderer/fallback; its scope does not replace the selected universe-model closure.
HYG is a compact astronomical star catalogue with share-alike data licensing; the selected YEIS snapshot already includes a derived compact binary and its required attribution.

search_ladder.conclusion: The whole YEIS product exists and is already selected as the source mother, but importing the complete application would retain simulator UI, tours, missions and hundreds of MB of unrelated media.
The reusable engine/model subset can live under the existing Astro/React shell; a dependency scan proves the model closure is small enough to vendor directly without the full product runtime.
Universe/StarSystem/StarCatalog/SystemGenerator form the required subsystem; ProceduralPlanets stays separate as an optional renderer rather than duplicating the model layer.
The 109,401-star compact HYG-derived binary and name table are reusable data assets when copied with their CC BY-SA notice.

coverage_matrix.decision: Vendoring records the exact source SHA beside copied files while avoiding runtime dependence on the changing upstream repository.
The measured closure is 22 TypeScript files plus ~2.83 MB catalog data, far smaller than the full application.
A local adapter keeps the existing product shell and allows later renderer migration independently.
Keep the already-proven one-method registerExtraSystem patch in the vendored Universe class and put Personal Universe Hero definitions outside vendor code.

coverage_matrix.capability: upstream algorithms remain recognizable for future audit
coverage_matrix.decision: Copy source mostly verbatim and isolate three host patches in a PATCHES.md rather than translating algorithms into new local code.
Vendored TypeScript is handled by the existing Astro/Vite build and requires no submodule bootstrap or nested web app.

candidates.name: Vendor exact 22-file YEIS core closure + data assets + adapter
candidates.license: MIT source; HYG-derived catalog CC BY-SA 4.0; notices retained
candidates.reason: Maximizes verified reuse while preserving the personal shell, keeps the dependency boundary small, and has already passed a Three 0.185.1 compatibility compile with only explicit host shims.

candidates.name: Pin the complete YEIS repository as a Git submodule
candidates.license: MIT source at pinned commit; third-party notices retained
candidates.reason: Pins provenance cleanly but carries the entire app/media/source tree and adds clone/deploy initialization complexity for code that is intentionally not part of the product.

candidates.name: Embed a built YEIS application as an iframe/microfrontend
candidates.license: MIT source at pinned commit; third-party notices retained
candidates.reason: Fast visual reuse but creates a second application/runtime, weakens shared navigation/Hero-state integration and keeps upstream simulator UI instead of the personal product shell.

candidates.name: Translate YEIS model algorithms into the existing V2 generator types
candidates.source: local V2 plus upstream YEIS reference
candidates.license: Project code derived from MIT algorithms
candidates.reason: Would recreate the exact model layer we selected YEIS to avoid rebuilding, increase diff/audit cost and make future upstream comparison harder.

candidates.name: Reuse the YEIS compact HYG-derived catalog assets unchanged
candidates.license: CC BY-SA 4.0 data; attribution/share-alike notice retained
candidates.reason: The binary is already the exact compact format StarCatalog expects, contains 109,401 stars and avoids creating another star-data preprocessing pipeline.

decision.rationale: Vendor only the proven model/data closure from the pinned MIT commit, keep upstream structure recognizable, isolate host-specific patches and expose it through a Personal Universe adapter. This gets the mature real/procedural universe model into the project now without committing to the upstream UI/render loop or duplicating algorithms.

higher_level_tradeoffs.reason: The complete repository is broader but its extra product UI, lessons, tours, missions and media provide negative global value for this site; the measured 22-file closure captures the needed engine capability with much less coupling.

Embedding the whole application gives broad immediate visuals but creates a second product runtime and blocks clean shared Hero/navigation state, so the narrower engine extraction has higher end-to-end value.

decision.fallback: If the vendored closure later proves too tightly coupled, retain it as a compatibility module and migrate only its public model interfaces behind the same adapter; do not fall back to copying current AGPL upstream code.
